text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000109 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation across every complexity stratum, but documentation is too thin to say whether the high codes are supported.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share is not confined to sicker patients: the by-complexity table shows rates above the all-provider share in every condition band, including 0- and 1-condition patients, and the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include routine-looking diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection (C0059105, C0059772), urinary tract infection (C0059353, C0059638) and follow-up encounters (C0058980). That pattern is more consistent with upcoding than with a uniformly complex panel, although the provider's heavy 99214 use and the many multi-morbid 99215 patients (e.g., C0058952, C0059911) show part of the panel is genuinely complex. The records review is the key gap: only two 99215 claims were documented, both supported at high MDM (including low-complexity claim C0059173), and no data-reviewed inflation signal appeared, so the chart evidence neither supports nor undercuts the statistical flag. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims (zero- and one-condition patients with acute or follow-up diagnoses) to test whether MDM and time actually support level 5, then extend the request to a larger random sample of 99215 claims."}
